aaa_enabled.summary: Enable the AAA subsystem, then define authentication methods before disconnecting.
aaa_enabled.notes: Enabling AAA changes login behaviour immediately. Configure 'aaa authentication login' with a local fallback in the same session to avoid lockout.

secure_vty_transport.summary: Restrict every VTY line to the SSH transport.
secure_vty_transport.notes: Evaluated worst-case across all 'line vty' blocks: if any block permits a cleartext transport, the control fails.

vty_idle_timeout.summary: Set an idle timeout of 10 minutes or less on every VTY line.
vty_idle_timeout.notes: Evaluated worst-case: the longest timeout configured across VTY lines is used, and any 'exec-timeout 0' is treated as no timeout at all.

enable_secret_encrypted.summary: Configure a hashed enable secret and turn on password encryption; remove the legacy enable password.
enable_secret_encrypted.notes: CIS lists these as two clauses; they are evaluated together here because either one alone still leaves privileged credentials recoverable. 'service password-encryption' uses reversible Vigenere (type 7) encoding and is a defence-in-depth measure, not a substitute for 'enable secret'.

no_default_snmp_community.summary: Remove default community strings and replace them with unique, non-guessable values restricted by an ACL.
no_default_snmp_community.notes: Comparison is case-insensitive: 'Public' is no less well-known than 'public'. Prefer SNMPv3 with authPriv over any v1/v2c community.

http_server_disabled.summary: Disable the HTTP server; use HTTPS or SSH if a management interface is genuinely required.
http_server_disabled.notes: Mapped at section level: this control is expressed under the benchmark's global service rules, and the exact clause number differs between IOS 15 and IOS 17 editions. Confirm the clause against your licensed copy before citing it in a formal audit.

ssh_version_2.summary: Generate an adequate RSA key and pin SSH to version 2.
ssh_version_2.notes: An absent 'ip ssh version' statement is reported as NEEDS_REVIEW rather than FAIL: the effective version depends on the IOS train and on whether an RSA key exists, so it cannot be established from the configuration text alone.

logging_enabled.summary: Enable logging to a sized local buffer and to a remote syslog collector.
cli: service timestamps log datetime msec show-timezone
logging_enabled.notes: CIS treats the buffer and the remote host as separate clauses; this rule requires at least one destination and fails the device if logging is explicitly turned off with 'no logging on'.

management_acl.summary: Permit only the management network, and apply the list inbound on every VTY line.
management_acl.notes: Verify your own address is inside the permitted range before applying this, and keep console access available: an access-class that excludes you locks you out of the device. This control is evaluated worst-case - one VTY block without an inbound access-class fails it, because that block is the way in.

login_banner.summary: Set a login banner stating that access is restricted and activity is monitored.
cli: Authorised access only. Activity is logged and monitored.
login_banner.notes: Do not name the device, its model, its owner or its software version in the banner: that is free reconnaissance. Have the wording approved by whoever owns legal risk in your organisation.

password_min_length.summary: Enforce a minimum length for every locally configured password.
password_min_length.notes: This applies to passwords set after the command, not to existing ones. Re-set existing local credentials afterwards, or the control passes while short passwords remain in use.

ntp_configured.summary: Point the device at two or more internal time sources.
ntp_configured.notes: Two sources let the device detect a lying one; a single source is a single point of failure for every timestamp it produces. Authenticate NTP (ntp authenticate / ntp trusted-key) where the time source crosses an untrusted network.

no_write_snmp_community.summary: Remove every read-write community; use read-only with an ACL, or SNMPv3 for write access.
no_write_snmp_community.notes: This is independent of the community's name: renaming a read-write community away from 'private' does not fix it. If write access is genuinely required, use SNMPv3 with authPriv rather than a v2c community.
